purpose: Native NAM MIS on/off-ramp surface appearance compared with the retained DD RHW-4 materials.
scope: Audited source resources and their decoded texture identities only; custom geometry, slopes, connectivity, and in-game rendering require separate checks.
privacy: Private archive paths and native binary payloads are omitted.

authored_mapping.ramp: Central native MIS pavement strip with original physical texture scale and directed white/yellow edge markings.
authored_mapping.high_collar: The same continuous native MIS pavement strip as the ramp; retained native DD RHW-4 mainline faces keep their original material.
authored_mapping.concrete: Unmodified native substructure material with spatial UV coordinates.
authored_mapping.barrier: Unmodified native barrier material with measured side and top texture strips.
authored_mapping.pavement_owner: Join each directed ramp and ground-turn pair at its exact mouth, then select one connected road for each triangle and project all three vertices onto that same road.
authored_mapping.ground_apron: Use the unmarked wheel-track and grey asphalt strip of the same native MIS texture, U=0.375..0.59375 across the 3.5 m turn width; smoothly end raised-ramp edge paint over pavement heights 1.5..0 m.

apron_uv_regression.scope: Actual authored ground-apron triangles after exact planar texture subdivision, before float32 S3D encoding; the physical surface and traffic remain unchanged.
apron_uv_regression.quantity: Texture-coordinate distance divided by planar edge length, in repeats per metre.
apron_uv_regression.limit_scope: A curved 6 m collar contains a tighter inner texture radius than a straight road; this bound permits its spatial variation, while rejecting the reproduced disconnected-fragment phase jump.

ground_texture_tessellation.scope: Flat authored apron asphalt only; retained native faces, physical pavement, routes, construction ownership, and resource identities are unchanged.
ground_texture_tessellation.subdivision: Exact edge midpoints on the existing plane, retaining the original winding and binary coordinates.
